name: Obsidian-Gate
description: Obsidian-Gate takes its name from the structure that dominates its northern hemisphere—a ring of black stone two kilometers in diameter, standing perfectly vertical on a plain of fused glass. The ring predates any known civilization by millions of years, its material composition matching nothing in the surrounding geology, its surface unmarked by the impacts that have cratered everything else. Through its center, space behaves incorrectly, light bending in patterns that suggest passage to somewhere else.

The glass plains surrounding the Gate extend for hundreds of kilometers, evidence of whatever event accompanied its creation or arrival. The heat required to fuse this much surface material exceeds anything natural, suggesting energies deliberately applied. The canyon systems that radiate outward from the Gate follow perfectly straight lines, as if carved by the same force that vitrified the surrounding landscape. Whatever happened here was intentional and precise.

The spatial distortion within the Gate fluctuates unpredictably, sometimes showing what appear to be star fields from different regions of space, sometimes displaying nothing at all, sometimes revealing glimpses of structures that don't exist on any known world. Probes sent through have never returned, their telemetry cutting off instantaneously upon crossing the threshold. Yet the Gate clearly leads somewhere—the energy readings suggest active transit potential rather than mere anomaly.

Research installations maintain safe distance while studying the Gate obsessively, the potential applications of a functional wormhole beyond calculation. Military interests have established presence as well, the strategic implications of instantaneous transit too significant to ignore. But the Gate remains inscrutable, its activation requirements unknown, its destination uncertain, its purpose forever unclear. It stands open and waiting, an invitation or a trap, a door that leads to revolution or annihilation. No one has found the courage or the desperation to step through and learn which.
